title: Rapid setup walkthrough: hero frames + data-driven visuals for Dedicated capacity
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a compact, progressive 'rapid setup' walkthrough for Dedicated capacity that surfaces capacity sizing, autoscaling policy choices, and an approachable SLA overview. Deliverables include responsive hero frames (desktop + tablet), three inline screenshot variants, a predictive-cost sparkline visual, an autoscale policy selector illustration, and a compact SLA status strip. The flow should be usable in the Console quickstart modal and the onboarding checklist page.
acceptance_criteria: Hero frames (desktop + tablet) exported as 2x PNG and SVG, matching Console color tokens
Predictive-cost sparkline implemented as a simple data-driven illustration with hover tooltip spec
Autoscale policy visual has three presets (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive) with microcopy explaining trade-offs
SLA overview compact strip communicates uptime target, typical p95 latency, and fallback policy in <90 characters
Design handoff in Figma with component tokens, responsive constraints, and a short dev QA checklist
tasks: Draft wireframes for 3-step rapid setup flow (capacity slider, policy selector, SLA summary)
Design detailed hero frames and export assets
Create hover tooltip copy for predictive-cost sparkline and batch-sizing hints
Sync with Runtime Eng on kernel/latency constraints to set realistic p95 targets
Prepare Figma handoff and Jira/Linear comments for dev implementation
Run 1 usability micro-test with 5 engineers and capture feedback
comments: 2026-02-21 Maya Chen: Initial wireframes uploaded to Figma; recommended starting with a compact 3-card layout to keep modal height small.
2026-02-25 Liam O'Connor: Reviewed wireframes. Eng feedback: predictive-cost sparkline should assume batching behavior (use 'typical' and 'peak' lines). Need exact metric names from Runtime team.
2026-02-27 Priya Nambiar (PM): PM preference for 'Balanced' preset to be default. Add a one-line rationale that mentions latency vs cost trade-off.

2026-03-03 Backend Eng (Mateo Ruiz): Confirmed p95 latency targets: 120ms for small models, 220ms for medium, 450ms for large under Dedicated baseline. Suggested showing relative ranges instead of exact numbers to avoid hard promises.

2026-03-06 Design review: Minor copy changes approved. Ask from legal to avoid SLA language that implies monetary penalties — change wording to 'SLO-backed availability' and link to SLA doc in enterprise plans.
2026-03-09 Usability test notes: 5 engineers; two misinterpreted the autoscale 'burst' toggle — added inline microcopy and a concise example line ('handles 10k QPS bursts for ~5 minutes').

2026-03-10 Liam O'Connor: Preparing Figma handoff. Export tokens and mark assets with export naming conventions for Console pipeline. Creating basic CSS snippets for sparkline colors and stroke widths.
